experiments.design: Repeat matched Bell trials using independent QRNG technologies and independently audited setting pipelines.
experiments.discriminator: A candidate model must predict a quantitative difference between generator classes before data collection.
experiments.limitation: A null difference does not rule out unrestricted common-cause models.
experiments.name: Independent setting-generator comparison
experiments.question: Do Bell statistics change when the physical setting generator changes?

experiments.design: Use astronomical photon properties to determine measurement settings while maintaining spacelike separation.
experiments.discriminator: Constrains specified past-common-cause models and their allowed causal regions.
experiments.limitation: Does not eliminate all superdeterministic explanations.
experiments.name: Cosmic setting-source Bell test
experiments.question: How far into the past can plausible common-cause explanations be constrained?

experiments.design: Use a measurement-dependent local inequality with independently characterised setting-generation statistics.
experiments.discriminator: Rejects local models above a preregistered measurement-dependence bound.
experiments.limitation: The result constrains model classes; it does not directly observe hidden variables.
experiments.name: Measurement-dependent inequality test
experiments.question: How much measurement independence is compatible with observed Bell correlations?

experiments.design: Repeat a matched Bell protocol while changing source, setting-generation and detection spacetime arrangement.
experiments.discriminator: Only useful if competing models provide distinct quantitative predictions for each geometry.
experiments.limitation: Changing geometry alone does not distinguish models with unrestricted hidden correlations.
experiments.name: Spacetime configuration comparison
experiments.question: Do alternative causal geometries yield different model predictions?

experiments.design: Use a preregistered human-generated setting protocol and a measurement-dependent Bell inequality.
experiments.discriminator: Compare with preregistered bounds for explicitly parameterised local models.
experiments.limitation: Human choices do not logically prove measurement independence.
experiments.name: Human-generated setting comparison
experiments.question: Does a model accommodate a distinct setting-generation process?

general_limitations: Hidden variable lambda is not directly observed.
A Bell violation alone does not identify a unique causal mechanism.
Unrestricted measurement-dependent models can be unfalsifiable.
Each candidate must preregister quantitative predictions.
